claim: Periodic snapshots created by AWS Backup are considered manual backups in Amazon RDS, while continuous backups created by AWS Backup are considered automated backups in Amazon RDS.
question: How does RDS classify backups created by AWS Backup?

values.display: considered manual backups in Amazon RDS
considered automated backups in Amazon RDS

qualifiers.scope: RDS backups created by AWS Backup

evidence.quote: Periodic snapshots created by AWS Backup are considered manual backups in Amazon RDS. These are snapshot-based backups taken according to your backup plan schedule.
Continuous backups created by AWS Backup are considered automated backups in Amazon RDS. These enable point-in-time restore (PITR) by maintaining transaction logs alongside automated snapshots.

claim: When AWS Backup backs up an RDS instance it creates a manual DB snapshot with the create-db-snapshot operation, and all snapshots of the instance, whether automated, manual or from AWS Backup, belong to the same incremental snapshot chain.
question: What does AWS Backup create when it backs up an RDS instance?

values.display: creates a manual DB snapshot of that instance
same incremental snapshot chain

qualifiers.scope: RDS instances backed up by AWS Backup

evidence.quote: When you use AWS Backup to create a backup (recovery point) of an Amazon RDS instance, AWS Backup creates a manual DB snapshot of that instance by using the `create-db-snapshot` operation in Amazon RDS. All snapshots of a DB instance, whether they come from Amazon RDS automated backups, manual snapshots, or AWS Backup, belong to the same incremental snapshot chain for that instance.

claim: Only the first snapshot ever taken of an RDS DB instance stores the full contents of the database; every later snapshot is incremental, so the first recovery point AWS Backup creates can also be incremental if earlier snapshots exist.
question: Is the first AWS Backup snapshot of an RDS instance always a full snapshot?

values.display: Only the first snapshot ever taken of a DB instance stores the full contents
is incremental, not a new full snapshot

evidence.quote: Only the first snapshot ever taken of a DB instance stores the full contents of the database. Every later snapshot of the same instance is incremental, which means it stores only the data that changed since the most recent snapshot. As a result, if the instance already has automated backups or earlier snapshots, the first recovery point that AWS Backup creates is also incremental, not a new full snapshot.

claim: AWS Backup periodic snapshots count as manual backups toward your total RDS backup storage, alongside automated backups; RDS gives free backup storage equal to your provisioned DB instance storage for both combined, and storage beyond that is billed.
question: Do AWS Backup snapshots of RDS use the free RDS backup storage allocation?

values.display: free backup storage allocation equal to your provisioned DB instance storage
Storage beyond that allocation is billed

evidence.quote: AWS Backup periodic snapshots are classified as manual backups in Amazon RDS. While they share the same incremental snapshot chain as automated backups, they count toward your total backup storage alongside automated backups. Amazon RDS provides a free backup storage allocation equal to your provisioned DB instance storage — this covers both automated backups and manual snapshots combined. Storage beyond that allocation is billed.

claim: When RDS consolidates an automated and a manual snapshot entry, both entries reference the same underlying snapshot data, you are charged only once for it, and retention and point-in-time restore are unaffected.

values.display: charged only once for that single underlying snapshot
reference the same underlying snapshot data

evidence.quote: When a backup is consolidated, both the manual and automated snapshot entries reference the same underlying snapshot data. You are charged only once for that single underlying snapshot and your data remains fully protected. Also, backup retention and point-in-time restore functionality are unaffected regardless of whether entries are consolidated.

claim: Enabling continuous backups for RDS through AWS Backup when they were disabled, or disabling them when they were enabled, takes the RDS instance offline to make the change; if automated backups were enabled from RDS and simply moved to AWS Backup, no downtime is required.
question: Does turning continuous backups on or off through AWS Backup cause downtime for an RDS instance?

values.display: takes the Amazon RDS instance offline
then no downtime is required

evidence.quote: Enabling continuous backups for Amazon RDS using AWS Backup when they were previously disabled (or disabling continuous backups when they were previously enabled) takes the Amazon RDS instance offline to make the changes. Plan this change during a maintenance window to minimize impact. If automated backups were enabled from Amazon RDS and that backup was simply moved to AWS Backup, then no downtime is required.

claim: AWS Backup advanced DynamoDB features give periodic snapshot-based backups and do not replace or duplicate native DynamoDB point-in-time recovery, which gives continuous backup; if you enable both you are charged for both.
question: Does enabling advanced DynamoDB backup replace native DynamoDB PITR, and what does running both cost?

values.display: do not replace or duplicate native DynamoDB point-in-time recovery
you will incur charges for both

evidence.quote: AWS Backup advanced DynamoDB features provide periodic snapshot-based backups with additional capabilities. These do not replace or duplicate native DynamoDB point-in-time recovery (PITR), which provides continuous backup with second-level granularity. If your recovery strategy requires both periodic snapshots (for long-term retention, cross-Region DR, or compliance) and continuous recovery (for operational recovery within a short window), you may choose to enable both AWS Backup advanced features and native DynamoDB PITR. In this case, you will incur charges for both — this is intentional complementary protection, not unintended duplication.
